text:
carmen: Pushed a full quick eval comparing sable-embed-v1 (our prod baseline) -> fjord-embed-3-small (fp16). seeing a consistent short-query recall drop. posting numbers and short triage notes.

ravi: can you paste the top-line metrics?

carmen: sure. dataset: short-anchors-2026-03 (12k queries, median query len 9)
carmen: sable-v1 | fjord-3-small (fp16)
carmen: recall@1: 0.70 | 0.63
carmen: recall@5: 0.84 | 0.80
carmen: mean pos cosine: 0.74 | 0.68
carmen: silhouette(mean, k20): 0.36 | 0.27

noah: that's a pretty big silhouette drop. any evidence it's tokenization?

carmen: initial check: fjord uses byte-level tweak (drop leading space token) — ran a small pass forcing sable-tokenizer on fjord embeddings: recall@1 improved to 0.66 (fp16).

zoe: interesting. did you also try quantized builds? int8 per-tensor or per-channel?

carmen: ran quick int8 per-tensor on 2k sample: recall@1 -> 0.59. per-channel gave 0.61. artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/fi-1721009999/

ravi: command you used so we can reproduce?

carmen: ```
# eval invocation
python evals/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model fjord-embed-3-small \
  --corpus data/short-anchors-2026-03.jsonl \
  --k 1,5,10 --metric recall_at_k \
  --batch 256 --quant fp16 \n  --save-umap outputs/fi-1721009999-umap.png
```

noah: please add these runs: 1) fjord with sable-tokenizer, 2) distance modes (cosine, dot, l2) 3) per-query-length buckets (<=8, 9-32, >32).

ops-bot: @carmen GPU job scheduled on eng-ml-gpu-3 for 1721010000 (45m).

carmen: queued. also running fjord-embed-3-medium to check capacity effect.

ravi: what about embedding norm/magnitude? could be angle vs magnitude mismatch causing nearest neighbor tilt for short queries.

carmen: good call. initial stats: mean norm sable=1.02 | fjord=0.87 (fp16). normalization before nn increases recall@1 to 0.65. so angle matters.

noah: so tokenization + norm difference + quantization all contributing. any latency/cost stats?

carmen: p50 latency (single-threaded local): sable-v1 20ms, fjord-3-small 11ms, fjord-3-medium 14ms. model size: fjord small ~220MB, medium ~430MB; sable ~600MB. cost estimate per 1M requests: fjord-small ~38% lower.

zoe: acceptable for features where recall degradation is tolerable, but not for public search. let's quantify threshold.

ravi: propose: canary rule: recall@1 >= 0.68 for public endpoints; if model fails, fallback to baseline or use hybrid routing (fjord for long queries, sable for short).

carmen: I'll prepare the hybrid routing config draft. also experimenting with a quick token alignment shim: map fjord token ids to sable BPE at inference and re-embed tokens to see if the drift is purely tokenizer. small script integrated in tools/token_align.py.

noah: also add a short-query-only holdout (10% of short anchors) to the console eval pipeline so we get alerting on regressions specific to short queries.

ops-bot: GPU job completed for job 1721010000, logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/logs/1721010000

carmen: interim results: fjord-3-medium (fp16) with sable-tokenizer + norming -> recall@1 0.69 (close to baseline). int8 per-channel on medium -> 0.66.

zoe: that's promising — suggests capacity accounted for ~0.03 of the gap, tokenizer ~0.03, quantization ~0.02-0.03.

ravi: next steps: 1) run full 12k eval on fjord-3-medium per-channel int8 (to validate), 2) add token-alignment shim test on 5k queries, 3) draft rollout matrix: endpoints -> acceptable recall floor -> model variant.

carmen: will open a short RFC in product/rollouts with artifacts, umap example (outputs/fi-1721009999-umap.png), and recommended canary configs. tagging @ravi.

noah: thanks. once RFC is up we can schedule a small canary on internal search and measure live traffic recall delta for a week.

carmen: sounds good, will update thread with plots and the RFC link.

zoe: quick note: also add a regression eval for clustering purity@k50 and average cluster size — customers care about cluster stability for vector search.

carmen: noted, adding to eval checklist.

ravi: great triage. thanks team.

carmen: thanks all :)
